channel.title: The Clanton Advertiser - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Clanton Advertiser (clantonadvertiser.com)

item.title: Column: Seeing the AHSAA reclassification from both sides
item.description: Alabama’s high school sports body has approved a first-ever public-private postseason split, and coaches, players and the author weigh its pros and cons under the new classifications.

item.title: County Queens help Jemison Library with a Fairytale Night
item.description: Chilton County queens brought storybook characters to life at Jemison Library’s 14th Fairytale Show, raising about $800 plus a $10,000 grant to support new books and free programs.

item.title: Fluttering About — Butterfly Bridge surpasses Flutter fundraising goal
item.description: Butterfly Bridge Children’s Advocacy Center’s Flutter 2026 tops its fundraising goal, drawing 300+ attendees and an estimated $170,000 to support free child advocacy services.

item.title: Next steps — Maplesville’s Crowe and McGee sign to different colleges
item.description: Maplesville softball standouts Hannah Crowe and Jaden McGee sign with Marion Military Institute and Southern Union, eyeing one more chance at a state title.

item.title: Goals galore for CCHS soccer teams in opening week
item.description: CCHS boys roll to 4-0 and 7-2 wins, while the girls notch a 6-1 victory matching last year’s win total as Tigers soccer opens the 2026 season with goals galore.

item.title: Jemison boys make history, Maplesville returns to sub-regionals in area tournament fallout
item.description: Jemison High School boys reach sub-regionals for first time in nearly 60 years, while Maplesville’s boys and girls also advance to next round during area basketball tournaments.

item.title: CCS continues to pull in funds while providing free meals for all students
item.description: Chilton County Schools now serves free breakfast and lunch to every student through a federal program that has saved families $9.9 million and added nearly $2 million to the system’s general fund.

item.title: Column: The only time to get married in Chilton County
item.description: A column narrows “acceptable” wedding dates to a few summer weekends, after ruling out football season, holidays, allergies and tornadoes.

item.title: Column: Can God Change His Mind?
item.description: Can God change His mind? This column explains how Scripture's portraits of “divine regret” fit with classic Christian doctrines of God's unchanging nature and perfect knowledge.

item.title: United Way establishes Chilton County Centennial Park near YMCA
item.description: United Way of Central Alabama is building an ADA-compliant Centennial Park near the Chilton County YMCA with playgrounds, gardens and an outdoor classroom, expected to open in spring to early summer.
